questions.question: Why does the mini agent work on a temporary copy of the repository?
options: So the original files are never modified; you review the diff and decide whether to apply it
Tests only run in temp folders
questions.explanation: Isolation plus a diff turns the agent's work into something you review, like a pull request.

questions.question: What does Workspace.verified require?
options: A passing test run, no edits after it, and no changed test files
questions.explanation: All three are facts the harness observes; none depend on the model's message.

questions.question: The repo map first ranked tests/ above inventory/. Why, and what fixed it?
options: The task said 'test suite', so test files matched task words; sorting source files before tests fixed it
questions.explanation: Word overlap is crude. Source code is usually what the agent needs to see first.

questions.question: A shell command appends to a test file and the user approved it. What status does the run get?
questions.explanation: The hash check catches test changes through any route, approved or not.

questions.question: llama3.2 (3B) answered with 'Here's the corrected code: …' but never called edit_file. What did the harness report?
questions.explanation: A fix described in prose isn't a fix. The diff and test evidence decide the status.

questions.question: The model called run_tests with an argument the tool doesn't take. What happened, and why is that the right behaviour?
options: The agent crashed, which is correct
The TypeError came back as an observation, so the model could retry without the argument
questions.explanation: Errors are observations. In run 1 the model retried correctly on the next step.
